title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2611.28854v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate participants in social experiments. Existing research has primarily focused on aligning social knowledge and isolated responses, while overlooking whether simulations can reproduce the collective effects of social interventions. This distinction is critical due to a failure mechanism we call a $bias$ $cascade$: similar individual states can lead to different actions, while agreement on isolated actions can still produce divergent outcomes through dynamic interactions. As a result, models may produce accurate social judgments yet fail to reproduce the outcomes of classic human studies. To investigate this problem empirically, we introduce $REFLEX$ (Reproducing Effects of Foundational Literature EXperiments), a benchmark of 30 counterfactual social experiments grounded in classic human studies that compares knowledge judgment with effect simulation. translated_title: 偏差级联：理解基于大语言模型的社会模拟中知识对齐与效应复现之间的差距
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于模拟社会实验中的参与者。现有研究主要集中于对齐社会知识和孤立响应，而忽视了模拟是否能够再现社会干预的集体效应。由于我们称之为“偏差级联”的失败机制，这一区别至关重要：相似的个体状态可能导致不同的行为，而对孤立行为的一致认同仍可能通过动态交互产生截然不同的结果。因此，模型可能产生准确的社会判断，却无法复现经典人类研究的结果。为了实证地研究这一问题，我们引入了REFLEX（基础文献实验效应复现）基准，该基准包含30个基于经典人类研究的反事实社会实验，用于比较知识判断与效应模拟。知识判断直接……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出“偏差级联”这一失败机制，并构建了包含30个反事实社会实验的REFLEX基准，揭示了大语言模型即使具备准确的社会知识判断能力，仍可能无法复现经典社会研究的集体干预效应。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies the "bias cascade" failure mechanism and introduces REFLEX, a benchmark of 30 counterfactual social experiments, revealing that LLMs can make accurate social knowledge judgments yet fail to reproduce the collective effects of classic human studies.
